analysis:
Examined the three base_text units of ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift together with the patch excerpt, which is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false). The visible changes are: (1) at head line 207, autopilotAllowsModel is replaced by autopilotServesModel in the load admission guard; (2) transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) calls are added at head lines 397 and 434; (3) reconcileAutopilotPlacements() is added in unloadModel after the slot is removed, at head lines 1148-1150; (4) head lines 1298-1306 change in a part of the patch I cannot see.

Security relevance: the load path preserves the T-041/T-012/T-027 mitigations unchanged. The weight-hash capture, post-load TOCTOU recheck and cache-eligible hash binding all remain in the base text, and none are touched by the visible hunks. Cache eligibility (cacheEligibleWeightHash) is still derived only from the verified artifact.

The predicate swap at line 207 is the only potential authorization-related change. It narrows or alters which models Autopilot permits. The definition of autopilotServesModel and the transitionGenerations semantics are not supplied, so I cannot confirm it does not widen loading beyond the previous policy. The model_not_selected guard still applies, and the explicit autopilot command-ID exception is unchanged.

The new reconcileAutopilotPlacements() call sits between the awaits in unloadModel and runs after modelsUnloading.remove. This could create a reentrancy window in which a new request reloads the model while the unload is still finishing. The code comment says the call is meant to prevent exactly that. Whether it actually does cannot be verified from the supplied text.

I found no concrete regression. Questions for integration: the autopilotServesModel versus autopilotAllowsModel semantics, the transitionGenerations.begin balance with a matching end on every error and cancel path (the visible catch block has no end call, so the matching end is presumably elsewhere), and the truncated hunks at head lines 1298-1306.
